title: Staged hotfix branching and rollback playbook for LTS & rolling channels
creator: Marco Liu
description: Purpose: define a reproducible, low-latency runbook for issuing emergency patches and performing safe rollbacks across Redwood Inference release channels (hosted rolling, dedicated reserved, and LTS/private deployments). This ticket captures severity criteria, branch naming conventions, automated backport tooling, canary/gradual rollout gates, verification checks, and communication templates. Goals: 1) reduce decision time to under 15 minutes for Sev1 regressions; 2) ensure every emergency patch has a clear backport matrix and an automated CI job that validates cherry-picks; 3) provide deterministic rollback paths that minimize data loss and avoid inconsistent client contracts.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Severity rubric with examples is documented and approved by SRE and Product
A2: Branching convention and naming scheme published in Confluence and enforced by repo pre-commit hooks
A3: Automated cherry-pick/backport job (GH Actions) created that runs tests and KV-cache sanity checks across target branches
A4: Canary rollout plan template (percentages, metric thresholds, time windows) available and wired into console rollout UI
A5: Rollback checklist with monitoring playbook and communication templates verified in a tabletop run
backport_matrix: private/onprem builds: package-level patches (rpm/deb) produced from hotfix branches and published to private registry
Dedicated pools: use dedicated-image tags (dedicated-<commit>-hotfix) and ensure migration plan in console before rollout
severity_rubric: Sev1 (P0/high): Data corruption, auth/traffic-plane outage, model-serving incorrect semantics causing customer loss. Trigger: immediate incident bridge and hotfix path.

Sev2 (P1/medium): Significant latency regressions, degraded model outputs causing major feature breakage but with workarounds. Trigger: planned hotfix in next patch window or accelerated if regression increases.
Sev3 (P2/low): Cosmetic API changes, minor performance drops, or telemetry-only anomalies. Fix scheduled in normal release cadence.
branching_and_naming: Branch policy: always branch from the exact commit that corresponds to the deployed tag for that channel (use 'git show-ref -s <deployed-tag>')
For private/on-prem customers include customer tag in PR title and create a separate patch package: hotfix/release-1.18/customer-<acronym>/...
automation_and_ci: New GH Action: .github/workflows/hotfix-backport.yaml - runs against list of target branches provided in PR body, attempts cherry-picks, runs unit/integration/kv-cache sanity tests
Auto-approve fallback: backport job posts a summary comment with failed cherry-picks and suggested manual commands; automated cherry-picks must be marked 'auto-applied' before merging
Pre-merge checks: smoke tests against a staging image, canary simulation with traced tokens, and a token cost sanity check to detect accidental changes in batching behavior
rollout_gates_and_canary: Canary baseline: 1% traffic for 15 minutes -> validate error-rate < baseline + 0.5% & p95 latency not increased by > 20%
Gradual increments: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with manual approval at each gate (console rollouts feature to be used for hosted and dedicated)
Automatic abort: configured alarms on console (error-rate, successful response schema mismatch, cost-per-token spike) will automatically stop and rollback the rollout
Private deployments: provide a dry-run diff of model weights/quantization metadata and a migration checklist before enabling traffic shift
rollback_playbook_steps: 1) Detection & Triage: on alarm/incident, classify severity and open incident with ENG key (prefix INC-).
2) Containment: if the issue is channel specific, pause rollout & remove traffic from affected nodes or revert traffic-routing rule to previous model image tag.

3) Patch vs Rollback Decision: if root cause is small (<= 5 LOC) and patchable quickly, prepare hotfix branch; if systemic or unknown, perform safe rollback to last known good tag and open hotfix branch in parallel.
4) Build & Verify: produce artifacts (images, packages), run end-to-end smoke + KV cache migration validation and SLO verification in staging canary cluster.
5) Canary & Ramp: follow canary gates; monitor console metrics and tracing for new error patterns.
6) Rollback Execution: to rollback, use tagged images and run console rollback workflow; ensure database/schema compatibility checks are passed before traffic change.
7) Communication: Send status updates to #incidents and external customers (templates below), update status page, and schedule postmortem within 72 hours.
8) Postmortem: include timeline, decision log, and backlog items (tests, automation) to prevent recurrence.
communication_templates: Initial internal: [INC-<id>] Brief summary, impact, channels affected, lead engineer, mitigation in progress
External customer: Hello, we're investigating an issue affecting <feature>. We have paused the rollout and are working on a fix. We'll provide an update in 30 minutes.
Post-rollback: We rolled back to tag <tag>. Observed behavior restored to baseline. We will follow up with root cause and patch timeline.
runbook_checks_and_metrics: Essential metrics: request-error-rate, p50/p95 latency, kv-cache hit ratio, tokens-per-request distribution, cost-per-token delta
Verification scripts: repo/scripts/hotfix_verify.sh - runs integration tests and a synthetic request suite including long context and streaming paths
Monitoring playbook: dashboard template link and alert thresholds added to console - alert runbook must include on-call contact and escalation path
outstanding_decisions: D1: Finalize automatic rollback thresholds (current proposal: +0.5% absolute error-rate or 20% p95 latency increase).
D2: Whether to enable automated cherry-pick merges when all tests pass (security review flagged potential supply-chain risk).
D3: Decide retention window for hotfix branches and automatic cleanup policy (proposal: 180 days then archival).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated cherry-picks may introduce subtle behavioral regressions when code paths diverge across branches. Mitigation: require a full integration smoke with representative prompts and a synthetic model output diff.
Risk: Rollback may not be possible if DB migrations are non-reversible. Mitigation: avoid irreversible schema changes in hotfixes; if necessary, use feature flags and two-phase migrations.
Risk: Customer private deployments may lag; Mitigation: publish clear per-customer patch packages and a manual validation checklist.
